correctness.rationale: For the finite Heisenberg group over Z/n the exact-order-m central characters are precisely those borne by irreducibles of degree m; the Bump–Diaconis–Hicks–Miclo–Widom construction has (n/m)^2 φ(m) such irreps. Averaging their central spectral idempotents gives kernel c_m(t)/n with correct inverse translation. Their direct-sum eigenspaces have dimension n²φ(m), and distinct m are disjoint with total identity. Endpoint ℓ¹ and ℓ∞ norms are exactly total variation of the central kernel; 1/m Σ|c_m| factors over prime powers, yielding 2^ω(m)φ(m)/m. Subtracting its coefficient at identity gives complement 1+norm−2φ(m)/n. The product ∏_{p|m}2(1−1/p) equals one precisely when all prime divisors equal two, including m=1. Independently checked exact rational kernels and complement for all 2≤n≤36; supplied verify.py extends to 120, but the universal proof is from Fourier decomposition and CRT, not finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Endpoint norms only; not interior ℓ^p or general nilpotent groups.
Representation classification is used as published input, not independently reproved from first principles beyond its explicit irreducible character construction.
